_comment: ARMS known to SURVIVE on this branch, with the mechanism and what would kill each.
`ledger.json` beside this file does the same for JOURNEYS and has since the layer
was built. The arms had no equivalent, and the consequence is the one that
mechanism exists to prevent: honest survivors make the whole bite suite
permanently red, and a permanently red suite cannot tell a new regression from
the standing state. Every arm added afterwards inherits a RESULT: FAILED that
says nothing about itself, and the only way to read the run is for a human to
remember which lines were there yesterday — which is precisely the memory this
directory exists to replace.
THIS FILE FAILS IN FOUR DIRECTIONS AND REFUSES IN THREE MORE. An entry does not
silence an arm: the arm is still mutated, still measured, still printed and still
counted, under its own verdict word, and the ledgered count rides in the RESULT
line itself. What the entry stops is the exit code, and only while the arm goes
on surviving with the EXACT detail recorded here.
* a ledgered arm that is KILLED fails the run and demands the entry be deleted,
by name. The reason has evaporated and nobody has to remember.
* a ledgered arm that NEVER RAN fails. An entry legitimises a MEASUREMENT;
never-ran is the absence of one, and an entry that absorbed it would certify
a dead arm as a considered decision.
* a ledgered arm surviving with a DIFFERENT detail fails. A survival whose
numbers moved is a survival nobody has looked at.
* an unledgered survivor fails, exactly as before.
* an entry naming an arm `selftest.mjs` does not have, or disagreeing with the
arm about its `journey` or its `assertion`, or missing a field, or offering a
shrug where the diagnosis goes, REFUSES the suite outright — exit 2, no
verdict. `--check-ledger` asks that half in a second, without a build.
`selftest-verdict-test.sh` probe 7 produces all seven, for real, over synthetic
journals in a temporary directory. A defence nobody has watched fail is
indistinguishable from no defence, and this is the one defence in the directory
whose job is to make a red LEGITIMATE.
AN ENTRY IS THE LAST RESORT AND NOT THE FIRST. This file was opened with three
candidates and two of them were FIXED instead:
* `P2/the-path-leaves-the-page-as-well-as-the-row` was DEAD, not surviving. Its
`find` was the call-trace row's `tdiv` branch at the indentation that branch
had before `f388cdf` wrapped the row in an `if asSummary:`, so the string
occurred ZERO times, the arm scored NEVER RAN on every run, and journey 14
went on looking covered while nothing demonstrated that its path assertion
bites. Repaired — and widened to all three row shapes, because the assertion
it names has a floor of one over the whole pane and any surviving spelling
clears it. It now KILLS: `counted 0, the claim needs at least 1`.
* `O2/a-control-on-every-row` was not a survivor at all. It was a RACE, and it
is `FJ3`'s lesson arriving from the other side — FJ3 reported KILLED for its
whole life while being killed by a race rather than by its assertion. O2
SURVIVED on CI (run 34018128849, shard 4 of 8, at 9219b26) at `0 authored
control(s)` and KILLS on a workstation at feab986 at `5 authored control(s)`,
on the same corpus and the same pinned engine. The assertion it named counts
origin controls on the NO-SOURCE subject's live State pane; a control is
rendered per VALUE ROW, and `projectState` returns at `if result.note.len >
0: return` — before the loop that fills `origin` — for every state that is
not 'this position's values are in the store'. A pane that has not adopted
this position's locals therefore has zero rows, and `originControls === 0` is
true whatever the classifier does. NOTHING PRINTED THE ROW COUNT, so a
verdict over five rows and a verdict over none were written down
identically. Journey 07 now prints it, in the note and in that assertion's
own detail, and the arm is re-aimed at the assertion written for this exact
mutation on the source-bearing subject, where the population is asserted
non-empty two verdicts above it. It now KILLS deterministically: `6
control(s) against 2 classified of 6 values`.
AND ONE CANDIDATE IS REFUSED RATHER THAN FIXED OR LEDGERED, which is the third
outcome and the one that draws this file's boundary.
* `FL2/the-panes-move-before-the-values-arrive` is a FLAKE, not a survivor, and
an entry for it would be actively harmful. Measured on ONE tree, on ONE
machine, on one day: KILLED at `counted 1, the claim says 0` when run alone,
and SURVIVED in shard 1 of the eight-shard sweep an hour later. `README.md`
already carries the mechanism and both sides of it — the blink is a ~13 ms
gap against a 16.7 ms frame, so a LOADED machine composites the contradictory
frame and kills the arm (8 of 8 at load average 128) while an IDLE one does
not (survived 4 of 5 at load 7-19). The faster the machine, the less
observable the defect — which is equally true of the defect itself.
THE BOTH-DIRECTIONS RULE IS WHAT REFUSES IT, and that is the rule working
rather than a gap in it. An entry would legitimise whichever side happened to
be sampled the day it was written, and then FAIL with `THE REASON HAS
EVAPORATED` on every run that landed on the other side — turning an
intermittent red into a different intermittent red while claiming a decision
had been made. A ledgered survival must be a property of the CODE; FL2's is a
property of the scheduler. It needs an instrument that does not race, and the
one attempt on record (holding `ct/load-locals` replies back by 220 ms) was
reverted because it reddened the CORRECT tree 3 of 3 as well.
BEFORE WRITING AN ENTRY, ESTABLISH WHY THE ARM SURVIVES. Both of the above are
the same warning from opposite sides: a survivor is a finding to be diagnosed,
not a state to be recorded, and 'this arm has always killed' is weak evidence.
`why_it_survives` must name the code path and say why the mutation cannot reach
what the assertion reads; `killed_by` must name what would have to exist for the
arm to bite. An arm nobody can write those two sentences about has not been
diagnosed, and an undiagnosed arm is not eligible.
COUNT THE KEYS IN `known_survivors`; do not trust a sentence here about how many
there are. `ledger.json`'s own summary line has been wrong four times, which is
the register summarising itself wrongly — the one error these files cannot
afford.

P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.assertion: LIVE: on arrival the selection area names the frame the pane marks
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.why_it_survives:
THE CODE THE MUTATION REMOVES IS UNREACHABLE ON EVERY SURFACE THE JOURNEYS CAN DRIVE, and it is unreachable because three separate things now write the fact it stands behind.

The mutation deletes `session_view.selectionDetail`'s position fallback — the `if chosen < 0 and v.controls.positioned:` loop that picks the frame containing the position when no frame is MARKED. `chosen` is set by the loop above it, `for i, f in v.calltrace.frames: if f.current`, and `CallFrame.current` is `CalltraceVM.selectedEntry`. When that arm was written `selectedEntry` was read and never written, so on a hydrated session no frame was ever marked and the panel fell through to the source line with 49 frames on screen beside it. That is the defect the fallback exists for and it is real.

It has three writers now. `selectCalltraceFrame` on a row click; `selectLandingFrame` on the landing, added with `hydrate.paint`'s `Hydration.frameSeeded` gate; and inside `selectLandingFrame` the recovery ANCHOR path, `if anchor.len > 0 and s.selectCalltraceFrame(anchor): return true`, which returns BEFORE the position walk. On journey 14's live subject the anchor is what marks the frame, so a frame is current on arrival, the first loop always sets `chosen`, and the fallback beneath it is never consulted. Removing it changes nothing observable, which is what a survival on a correct assertion means.

THREE READINGS ESTABLISHED THIS RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT, and they are why the obvious repairs are ruled out. The arm survived the post-click panel assertion (`clicked="calculate_damage" panel="calculate_damage"` — the click writes the selection itself). It survived a newly added ARRIVAL assertion, which is the reading the fallback would have to be load-bearing for. And re-aiming the MUTATION at the landing seed's own position walk — `selectLandingFrame`'s `if lines.len == 0: return false` forced true, so the walk never runs — ALSO survived, at `counted 1, the claim says 1`, because the anchor had already marked the frame: a third writer standing behind the second.

WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not the O2 shape. O2 survived on one machine and killed on another because its population moved; this one has been measured SURVIVING on two machines, at two commits, in two different aims — CI run 34018128849 shard 5 of 8 at 9219b26, and a workstation at feab986 — and the survival is a property of the code, not of the schedule.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.killed_by:
A SUBJECT, NOT A STRONGER ASSERTION. The arm bites the moment the journeys can drive a live session in which no frame is marked on arrival: one reached WITHOUT a `call:` recovery anchor (so `selectLandingFrame`'s first branch does not return) whose `visibleLines` are empty at seed time (so its position walk finds nothing to select). With no `selectedEntry`, `selectionDetail`'s first loop leaves `chosen < 0`, and the removed fallback is exactly what decides whether the panel then names the frame the session is in or falls back to the source line — which is the assertion this arm names.

The honest alternative is to DELETE the fallback rather than ledger the arm, and it is refused deliberately: the fallback is live product code for a state the journeys cannot currently reach, and deleting shipped behaviour to make a mutation arm pass is the trade this whole layer exists to refuse. Add the subject; do not remove the code.

When either happens this arm is KILLED, this run FAILS demanding this entry be deleted, and nobody has to remember it was here.
